examination: Civil Services Mains Examination - Optional Subject

structure_note: Flat chronological numbered units, no lettered parts, so section_ref is omitted (rev2 M10). Units 1-10 cover modern India to Independence; 11-15 cover world history from the Enlightenment to the post-war order.
paper_title_note: paper_title MUST equal subjects.name for slug upsc-cse-mains-opt-history-p2 exactly.

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1. European Penetration into India: The Early European Settlements; The Portuguese and the Dutch; The English and the French East India Companies; their struggle for supremacy; Carnatic Wars; Bengal - The conflict between the English and the Nawabs of Bengal; Siraj and the English; The Battle of Plassey; Significance of Plassey.
micro_themes: Early European settlements; the Portuguese and the Dutch
The English and French East India Companies and their struggle for supremacy
The Carnatic Wars
Conflict between the English and the Nawabs of Bengal
Siraj-ud-Daula and the English; the Battle of Plassey and its significance

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2. British Expansion in India: Bengal - Mir Jafar and Mir Kasim; The Battle of Buxar; Mysore; The Marathas; The three Anglo-Maratha Wars; The Punjab.
micro_themes: Mir Jafar, Mir Kasim and the Battle of Buxar
Mysore and the Anglo-Mysore Wars
The Marathas and the three Anglo-Maratha Wars
Annexation of the Punjab

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 3 Early Structure of the British Raj
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 3. Early Structure of the British Raj: The Early administrative structure; From diarchy to direct control; The Regulating Act (1773); The Pitt's India Act (1784); The Charter Act (1833); The Voice of free trade and the changing character of British colonial rule; The English utilitarian and India.
micro_themes: Early administrative structure; from diarchy to direct control
The Regulating Act 1773 and Pitt's India Act 1784
The Charter Act 1833
Free trade and the changing character of British colonial rule
The English utilitarians and India

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 4 Economic Impact of British Colonial Rule
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 4. Economic Impact of British Colonial Rule: Land revenue settlements in British India; The Permanent Settlement; Ryotwari Settlement; Mahalwari Settlement; Economic impact of the revenue arrangements; Commercialization of agriculture; Rise of landless agrarian labourers; Impoverishment of the rural society; Dislocation of traditional trade and commerce; De-industrialisation; Decline of traditional crafts; Drain of wealth; Economic transformation of India; Railroad and communication network including telegraph and postal services; Famine and poverty in the rural interior; European business enterprise and its limitations.
micro_themes: Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems
Economic impact of the revenue arrangements
Commercialization of agriculture and the rise of landless labourers
Impoverishment of rural society
Dislocation of traditional trade and commerce; de-industrialisation
Decline of traditional crafts; drain of wealth
Railways, telegraph and postal communication
Famine and poverty in the rural interior
European business enterprise and its limitations

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 5. Social and Cultural Developments: The state of indigenous education, its dislocation; Orientalist-Anglicist controversy; The introduction of western education in India; The rise of press, literature and public opinion; The rise of modern vernacular literature; Progress of Science; Christian missionary activities in India.
micro_themes: State of indigenous education and its dislocation
The Orientalist-Anglicist controversy
Introduction of western education in India
Rise of the press, literature and public opinion
Rise of modern vernacular literature
Progress of science
Christian missionary activities in India

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 6. Social and Religious Reform movements in Bengal and Other Areas: Ram Mohan Roy, The Brahmo Movement; Devendranath Tagore; Iswarchandra Vidyasagar; The Young Bengal Movement; Dayanada Saraswati; The social reform movements in India including Sati, widow remarriage, child marriage etc.; The contribution of Indian renaissance to the growth of modern India; Islamic revivalism - the Feraizi and Wahabi Movements.
micro_themes: Ram Mohan Roy and the Brahmo movement
Devendranath Tagore and Iswarchandra Vidyasagar
The Young Bengal Movement
Dayananda Saraswati and the Arya Samaj
Social reform: sati, widow remarriage and child marriage
Contribution of the Indian renaissance to modern India
Islamic revivalism: the Feraizi and Wahabi movements

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 7. Indian Response to British Rule: Peasant movements and tribal uprisings in the 18th and 19th centuries including the Rangpur Dhing (1783), the Kol Rebellion (1832), the Mopla Rebellion in Malabar (1841-1920), the Santal Hul (1855), Indigo Rebellion (1859-60), Deccan Uprising (1875) and the Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900); The Great Revolt of 1857 - Origin, character, causes of failure, the consequences; The shift in the character of peasant uprisings in the post-1857 period; the peasant movements of the 1920s and 1930s.
micro_themes: Peasant movements and tribal uprisings of the 18th and 19th centuries
Rangpur Dhing, Kol Rebellion and Mopla Rebellion
Santal Hul, Indigo Rebellion, Deccan Uprising and Munda Ulgulan
The Great Revolt of 1857: origin, character and causes of failure
Consequences of the Revolt of 1857
Shift in the character of peasant uprisings after 1857
Peasant movements of the 1920s and 1930s

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 8 Factors leading to the birth of Indian Nationalism
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 8. Factors leading to the birth of Indian Nationalism: Politics of Association; The Foundation of the Indian National Congress; The Safety-valve thesis relating to the birth of the Congress; Programme and objectives of Early Congress; the social composition of early Congress leadership; the Moderates and Extremists; The Partition of Bengal (1905); The Swadeshi Movement in Bengal; the economic and political aspects of Swadeshi Movement; The beginning of revolutionary extremism in India.
micro_themes: Politics of association; foundation of the Indian National Congress
The safety-valve thesis
Programme, objectives and social composition of the early Congress
Moderates and Extremists
Partition of Bengal 1905 and the Swadeshi Movement
Economic and political aspects of the Swadeshi Movement
Beginning of revolutionary extremism in India

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 9 Rise of Gandhi and the Mass Movements
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 9. Rise of Gandhi; Character of Gandhian nationalism; Gandhi's popular appeal; Rowlatt Satyagraha; the Khilafat Movement; the Non-cooperation Movement; National politics from the end of the Non-cooperation movement to the beginning of the Civil Disobedience movement; the two phases of the Civil Disobedience Movement; Simon Commission; The Nehru Report; the Round Table Conferences; Nationalism and the Peasant Movements; Nationalism and Working class movements; Women and Indian youth and students in Indian politics (1885-1947); the election of 1937 and the formation of ministries; Cripps Mission; the Quit India Movement; the Indian National Army; the Naval Mutiny of 1946.
micro_themes: Rise of Gandhi; character of Gandhian nationalism and his popular appeal
Rowlatt Satyagraha and the Khilafat Movement
The Non-cooperation Movement
National politics between Non-cooperation and Civil Disobedience
The two phases of the Civil Disobedience Movement
Simon Commission, the Nehru Report and the Round Table Conferences
Nationalism and the peasant movements
Nationalism and working class movements
Women, youth and students in Indian politics 1885-1947
The election of 1937 and the formation of ministries
Cripps Mission and the Quit India Movement
The Indian National Army and the Naval Mutiny of 1946

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 10. Constitutional Developments in Colonial India between 1858 and 1935. 11. Other strands in the National Movement - The Revolutionaries: Bengal, the Punjab, Maharashtra, U.P, the Madras Presidency, Abroad; The Left - The Left within the Congress: Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose, the Congress Socialist Party; the Communist Party of India, other left parties. 12. Politics of Separatism - the Muslim League; the Hindu Mahasabha; Communalism and the politics of partition; Transfer of power; Independence.
micro_themes: Constitutional developments in colonial India, 1858-1935
Revolutionaries in Bengal, Punjab, Maharashtra, UP and Madras
Revolutionary activity abroad
The Left within the Congress: Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose, the Congress Socialist Party
The Communist Party of India and other left parties
The Muslim League and the Hindu Mahasabha
Communalism and the politics of partition
Transfer of power and Independence

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 11 Consolidation as a Nation and Caste Politics
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 13. Consolidation as a Nation; Nehru's Foreign Policy; India and her neighbours (1947-1964); The linguistic reorganisation of States (1935-1947); Regionalism and regional inequality; Integration of Princely States; Princes in electoral politics; the Question of National Language. 14. Caste and Ethnicity after 1947; Backward castes and tribes in post-colonial electoral politics; Dalit movements. 15. Economic development and political change; Land reforms; the politics of planning and rural reconstruction; Ecology and environmental policy in post-colonial India; Progress of science.
micro_themes: Nehru's foreign policy; India and her neighbours 1947-1964
Linguistic reorganisation of states
Regionalism and regional inequality
Integration of princely states; princes in electoral politics
The question of national language
Caste and ethnicity after 1947
Backward castes and tribes in post-colonial electoral politics; Dalit movements
Land reforms and the politics of planning and rural reconstruction
Ecology and environmental policy in post-colonial India
Progress of science after Independence

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 16. Enlightenment and Modern ideas: Major ideas of Enlightenment - Kant, Rousseau; Spread of Enlightenment in the colonies; Rise of socialist ideas (up to Marx); spread of Marxian Socialism.
micro_themes: Major ideas of the Enlightenment: Kant and Rousseau
Spread of Enlightenment in the colonies
Rise of socialist ideas up to Marx
Spread of Marxian socialism

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 13 Origins of Modern Politics and Industrialization
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 17. Origins of Modern Politics: European States System; American Revolution and the Constitution; French revolution and aftermath, 1789-1815; American Civil War with reference to Abraham Lincoln and the abolition of slavery; British Democratic Politics, 1815-1850; Parliamentary Reformers, Free Traders, Chartists. 18. Industrialization: English Industrial Revolution - Causes and Impact on Society; Industrialization in other countries: USA, Germany, Russia, Japan; Industrialization and Globalization.
micro_themes: The European states system
American Revolution and the Constitution
French Revolution and its aftermath, 1789-1815
American Civil War, Lincoln and the abolition of slavery
British democratic politics 1815-1850: reformers, free traders, Chartists
English Industrial Revolution: causes and impact on society
Industrialization in the USA, Germany, Russia and Japan
Industrialization and globalization

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 19. Nation-State System: Rise of Nationalism in 19th century; Nationalism: state-building in Germany and Italy; Disintegration of Empires in the face of the emergence of nationalities across the world. 20. Imperialism and Colonialism: South and South-East Asia; Latin America and South Africa; Australia; Imperialism and free trade: The new imperialism. 21. Revolution and Counter-Revolution: 19th Century European revolutions; The Russian Revolution of 1917-1921; Fascist Counter-Revolution, Italy and Germany; The Chinese Revolution of 1949.
micro_themes: Rise of nationalism in the 19th century
State-building in Germany and Italy
Disintegration of empires and the emergence of nationalities
Imperialism in South and South-East Asia
Imperialism in Latin America, South Africa and Australia
Imperialism and free trade: the new imperialism
19th century European revolutions
The Russian Revolution of 1917-1921
Fascist counter-revolution in Italy and Germany
The Chinese Revolution of 1949

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 15 World Wars, Decolonization and the Post-War World
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 22. World Wars: 1st and 2nd World Wars as Total Wars: Societal implications; World War I: Causes and consequences; World War II: Causes and consequences. 23. The World after World War II: Emergence of two power blocs; Emergence of Third World and non-alignment; UNO and the global disputes. 24. Liberation from Colonial Rule: Latin America-Bolivar; Arab world-Egypt; Africa-Apartheid to democracy; South-East Asia-Vietnam. 25. Decolonization and Underdevelopment: Factors constraining development, Latin America, Africa. 26. Unification of Europe: Post War Foundations: NATO and European Community; Consolidation and Expansion of European Community; European Union. 27. Disintegration of Soviet Union and the Rise of the Unipolar World: Factors leading to the collapse of Soviet communism and the Soviet Union, 1985-1991; Political Changes in East Europe 1989-2001; End of the cold war and US ascendancy in the World as the lone superpower.
micro_themes: The World Wars as total wars: societal implications
World War I: causes and consequences
World War II: causes and consequences
Emergence of two power blocs after 1945
Emergence of the Third World and non-alignment
The UNO and global disputes
Liberation from colonial rule: Latin America and Bolivar; the Arab world and Egypt
Africa from apartheid to democracy; South-East Asia and Vietnam
Decolonization and underdevelopment; constraints on development
Post-war foundations: NATO and the European Community
Consolidation and expansion of the European Community; the European Union
Collapse of Soviet communism and the Soviet Union, 1985-1991
Political changes in East Europe 1989-2001
End of the Cold War and US ascendancy as the lone superpower
